sections.html:
Hampton is a city with no county above it, out on the Virginia Peninsula. No county overlaps it, so the city itself mails your real estate tax bill. The 2020 census found 137,148 residents; the 2025 estimate is 137,315. Housing units totaled 62,444 and 7.7 percent were vacant, which makes for steady turnover.

Water covers about 62 percent of the city's area, and the ground sits around 10 feet above sea level on average, so flooding and flood insurance come up in most house conversations. Waterfront pockets such as Buckroe Beach and Fox Hill draw those questions first. Military moves around Langley Air Force Base and Fort Monroe also mean some owners sell on short notice, without time for repairs and showings.

The assessor decides value. The Treasurer sends bills and takes payment. Both keep offices at One Franklin Street. Reach the assessor in Suite 602 on 757-727-8311 and the Treasurer in Suite 100 on 757-727-6374. Every parcel is reappraised annually at full market value, and the city's tax year starts July 1 and ends June 30.

Real estate is taxed at $1.14 per $100 of assessed value. You can pay online, send a check, use the drop box at One Franklin Street, or call (877) 277-6341.

Two equal installments cover the year, on June 5 and December 5. Miss the date and a 10 percent penalty lands on the bill; unpaid balances also pick up interest at 10 percent a year starting July 1. Paying the entire year with the first installment is allowed.

Trust the due date printed on the bill itself. If a bill has not turned up as a due date nears, phone the Treasurer rather than waiting.

Owners can climb three rungs of review, and each clock starts on the date printed on the assessment notice.

LevelDeadlineWhat to know
Office Review30 days from the notice dateCall an appraiser first, as the city suggests
Board of Review60 days from the notice dateNo Office Review needed first; five Hampton owners may raise, lower or affirm the value
Circuit CourtPetition directlyNeither earlier step is required

The Board of Review hears cases mostly in May and June at the Ruppert Sargent Building. New construction or an addition triggers a supplemental assessment, with a 30-day appeal window from its notice. Call the assessor's office at 757-727-8311 before you file.

State law puts the real estate tax lien first among all liens, and in that statute penalties and interest are part of the tax. The settlement agent sends the Treasurer its money from your sale proceeds. Ask for a quote that stays valid through the closing date; interest keeps growing until the bill is actually paid.

  1. Call 757-727-6374 and request the balance for both installments.
  2. Ask whether a supplemental bill for an addition or new construction is coming.
  3. Hand the written quote to the title company.
  4. Tuck the paid receipt into your settlement file.

A merger on July 1, 1952 joined the city of Hampton, the town of Phoebus and Elizabeth City County into the single city of today. Older deeds and tax records can therefore mention Elizabeth City County or the town of Phoebus, and a seller with a family house should ask a title company to trace those names early.

Hampton traces its first English settlement to 1610 and became an independent city in 1908, so land records here run deep. Fort Monroe at Old Point Comfort was decommissioned as an army base on September 15, 2011, and the surrounding area has changed hands and uses since. If your parcel is near the fort or an old waterfront lot, a survey and a clean title search will save a buyer's attorney a lot of questions.

Hampton's neighborhoods range from Aberdeen Gardens and Farmington to Newmarket, Northampton and Hampton Woods, with Buckroe Beach and Fox Hill on the water. The Victoria Boulevard Historic District and Wythe, home of the Olde Wythe Historic District, are protected areas. Historic status can limit exterior changes, so a seller in Olde Wythe or Phoebus should ask city planning staff what applies to the address before promising a buyer anything.

Every year the city reappraises each property, so a notice can arrive without any change you made. When it comes, look first at the notice date, because both the 30-day and 60-day deadlines count from it. Next, set the new value beside recent sale prices of similar Hampton houses. A value that tracks the market is hard to argue with, while one that sits well above nearby sales is worth a call to an appraiser.

Describe condition honestly. An aging roof or a damp crawl space is something an appraiser may never see from the curb. Photos and a contractor's written estimate work better than a general complaint. If you win a reduction, the lower figure also becomes the number a buyer sees when they look up the property.

sections.h2: Splitting the year's bill at closing
sections.html:
Because Hampton bills in two installments and the tax year runs July 1 to June 30, a closing almost never lands on a clean boundary. Your sales contract states who owes which stretch, and the settlement statement shows the result as a credit or a charge. If the June installment was paid before you sell, expect the buyer to repay you for the days they own the house in that period. If the December installment is still open, the closing agent usually takes your share out of the proceeds and pays the Treasurer.

Ask the agent to show you the arithmetic line by line. A wrong date on the contract is the most common reason a proration looks off, and it is easy to fix before signing but hard to fix afterward.

sections.h2: What buyers check in a Hampton house
sections.html: With a humid climate and low elevation, inspectors look at roofs, gutters, crawl space moisture and the age of the air conditioning. Gather permits and receipts for that work before you list. Buyers also ask about commute routes: Interstates 64 and 664, the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel and the Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel are the usual ones. School zones follow the address, so send buyers to Hampton City Public Schools to confirm a zone instead of quoting one.

sections.h2: What to bring and how a cash sale differs
sections.html:
Bring your parcel details, the latest assessment notice and any tax bills to whichever office you visit. Inherited houses, rentals and dated homes are common sellers in this city. Cash Home Buyers CA buys Hampton houses as-is, which removes the repair list and the wait on a buyer's loan. The lien rule is unchanged, so any unpaid tax is still paid from your proceeds.

If you are deployed or transferred, ask the title company early what documents it needs from you.

faqs.q: What is the Hampton real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The city lists $1.14 per $100 of assessed value, with property assessed at 100 percent of market value.

faqs.q: When are Hampton real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5, in two equal installments. A 10 percent penalty applies after the due date.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Hampton assessment?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the notice date for an Office Review and 60 days for the Board of Review. You can petition the Circuit Court without either.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Hampton assessments?
faqs.a: Call the City Assessor at 757-727-8311. For payments and balances call the Treasurer at 757-727-6374.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hampton house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff from the Treasurer first.
